title: Requirements
subtitle: The cheapest bug to fix is the one caught before any code: get the right thing specified.

kinds.title: Functional and non-functional
kinds.body: Functional requirements say what the system does (“a user can reset a password by email”). Non-functional requirements constrain how: performance, security, usability, availability, portability. A good requirement is testable: “responds in under 2 s for 95 % of requests” not “fast”.

elic.title: Eliciting requirements
elic.body: Techniques: interviews, questionnaires, observation, workshops, prototypes, studying existing documents. Stakeholders disagree; requirements must be negotiated and prioritised (e.g. MoSCoW: must, should, could, won’t).

story.title: Use cases and user stories
story.body: A use case describes an actor achieving a goal in steps, with alternate flows for failures. A user story: “As a role I want goal so that benefit”, with acceptance criteria. Stories are small and estimated in points.

srs.title: The SRS
srs.body: A Software Requirements Specification (IEEE 830/29148) contains: introduction (purpose, scope, definitions), overall description (users, constraints), specific requirements (functional, external interfaces, performance, design constraints), and appendices. It must be complete, consistent, unambiguous, verifiable and traceable.

valid.title: Validation and change
valid.body: Validate by reviews, prototypes and test-case writing. Requirements change; manage change with a recorded process: request → impact analysis → approval → update and trace. Traceability links each requirement to design, code and tests.
valid.steps: A project has 120 requirements; 24 change after baseline. Volatility = 24/120.

fp.title: Sizing from requirements: function points
fp.body: Function points count user-visible functions: external inputs (EI), outputs (EO), inquiries (EQ), internal files (ILF), external interfaces (EIF), each weighted by complexity. Unadjusted FP = Σ count × weight; multiply by a value adjustment factor (0.65–1.35).
fp.steps: Average weights: EI 4, EO 5, EQ 4, ILF 10, EIF 7. Counts: EI 10, EO 6, EQ 5, ILF 4, EIF 2. UFP = 40 + 30 + 20 + 40 + 14.
